threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know you’re new when you still expect the Overground to run on time. Locals just shrug and check their phones for cider pop-up events instead.
Caught the 35 past Brixton Market, saw a guy doing a magic trick with a pack of cards. The bus was packed, but everyone suddenly wanted to watch.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a man in full lederhosen juggling beers outside a Kebab shop on Hermannstraße, I knew Neukölln had me hooked.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you catch trams holding spontaneous parties, complete with DJs and dance-offs, right in the middle of your commute.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to avoid 16th Street BART during delays. The rest are still standing there confused when the smoke rises.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy take a nap on the 31 Balboa while his burrito fell out of his lap. SFFD came by to pick it up, but he slept through it all.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the locals flock to the tiny bars with no signage for the best vermut in town.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the lack of pedestrian crossings on Carrer de Casanova, while still trying to find a shortcut.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of just 'the train.' Locals know it's a whole vibe, not just a commute.
Last night on the 133, a guy got on with a full saxophone and played ‘Careless Whisper’ while everyone pretended not to listen. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw a toddler playing in the street while their parents bartered with a döner guy—only in Neukölln do life and street food blend so perfectly.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a club that doubles as a former water pumping station, complete with rusty pipes and an underground vibe. Feels like a secret!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they can effortlessly name all the taco trucks that make it through the late-night fog without a GPS.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a bus driver call out a passenger for trying to sneak through the back. 'This isn’t a ninja movie!' It turned the whole bus into a giggling mess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the street performers are artists. Most are just trying to fund their next paella fix. The real talent hangs out in the back alleys.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their wide-eyed wonder at the late-night tapas bars, still oblivious to the locals' laid-back, almost tepid enthusiasm.
